english: For $\theta,\phi\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, let $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta,\phi)$ denote the unit vector which makes an angle $\theta$ with the $xy$-plane, has a positive $z$-component, and whose projection on the $xy$-plane makes an angle $\phi$ with the positive $x$-axis. Let $\theta_1,\theta_2,\phi_1,\phi_2\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ be such that $\tan\theta_1=\frac{3}{4}$, $\tan\theta_2=\frac{12}{5}$, $\tan\phi_1=\frac{4}{3}$ and $\tan\phi_2=\frac{7}{24}$. If $\psi$ is the angle between the vectors $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta_1,\phi_1)$ and $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta_2,\phi_2)$, then the value of $\cos\psi$ is ______.
hindi: $\theta,\phi\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ के लिए, माना कि $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta,\phi)$ वह मात्रक सदिश है जो $xy$-तल से $\theta$ कोण बनाता है, जिसका $z$-घटक धनात्मक है, तथा $xy$-तल पर जिसका प्रक्षेप धनात्मक $x$-अक्ष से $\phi$ कोण बनाता है। माना कि $\theta_1,\theta_2,\phi_1,\phi_2\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ इस प्रकार हैं कि $\tan\theta_1=\frac{3}{4}$, $\tan\theta_2=\frac{12}{5}$, $\tan\phi_1=\frac{4}{3}$ तथा $\tan\phi_2=\frac{7}{24}$ है। यदि सदिशों $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta_1,\phi_1)$ तथा $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta_2,\phi_2)$ के बीच का कोण $\psi$ है, तो $\cos\psi$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: A unit vector making angle $\theta$ with the $xy$-plane has $z$-component $\sin\theta$ (positive here) and a projection of length $\cos\theta$ on the $xy$-plane. That projection makes angle $\phi$ with the $x$-axis, so $\overrightarrow{u}(\theta,\phi)=\cos\theta\cos\phi\,\hat{i}+\cos\theta\sin\phi\,\hat{j}+\sin\theta\,\hat{k}$; its length is $\sqrt{\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta}=1$.

All angles are acute, so all ratios are positive: $\tan\theta_1=\frac34\Rightarrow\cos\theta_1=\frac45,\ \sin\theta_1=\frac35$; $\tan\theta_2=\frac{12}{5}\Rightarrow\cos\theta_2=\frac{5}{13},\ \sin\theta_2=\frac{12}{13}$.
originality_note: New: two directions given by elevation and azimuth (as in lines of sight); the dot product yields the vector form cos(psi) = cos t1 cos t2 cos(p1 - p2) + sin t1 sin t2, and the compound-angle formula evaluates the azimuth difference (way 5). Closest known: proving cos(A - B) by the dot product of two unit vectors in a plane. Different because: the vectors are in space, the plane result appears only as one factor, and four angles given by tangents must be combined.
blueprint_concepts: Vectors applied to prove trigonometric and geometric results

concept_use.Vectors applied to prove trigonometric a: The dot product of the two unit vectors written in elevation-azimuth form proves the angle formula cos(psi) = cos t1 cos t2 cos(p1-p2) + sin t1 sin t2.
concept_use.Compound angles: sin(A+/-B), cos(A+/-B),: cos(p1 - p2) = cos p1 cos p2 + sin p1 sin p2 = 4/5 from the given tangents.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, vector and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated the sign of the z-component and the reference axis for the projection so each vector is unique; all angles restricted to (0, pi/2) so the signs of the ratios are fixed. Changed: replaced an earlier design (unit vectors along the sides of a triangle, a known resultant-of-forces result) by this one.
key_step: Writing u(theta, phi) in components and recognising cos(p1-p2) inside the dot product.
justification: Routine chain: components of a direction, a dot product, a compound-angle evaluation and four ratio conversions; no insight beyond setting up the vector. Like the routine vector computation of 2026-P2-Q1 (L2).
